title: Lifting and removing the top residue cell of a complete complex
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l with its valuation ring, uniformizer and residue field [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let S be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] categorically weakly contractible for its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let K be a complete complex over its completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-derived-complete], whose residue has Tor interval [a,a+d], for a integer and d natural [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Supply a zero-differential finite-free cochain model R of its residue, with terms zero outside [a,a+d] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There is a distinguished triangle A to K to L to A[1] (allowing a specified isomorphism of its middle object with K) such that A has a finite free sheaf model concentrated only in degree a+d, L is complete, L is zero if d=0, and if d>0 the residue of L has a zero-differential finite-free cochain model supported in [a,a+(d-1)]. This is one cell removal, not a bounded model of K.

proof.text: The valuation ring $R$ is a principal ideal domain with nonzero uniformizer and finite residue field by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; in particular it is Noetherian since each ideal has one generator. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] to $R,(\varpi)$: $B_T$ is flat over the constant $R_T$ on any scheme $T$, and $B_T\otimes^L_{R_T}(R/\varpi^n)_T\simeq(R/\varpi^n)_T$. The constant sequence $0\to R_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R_T\to(R/\varpi^n)_T\to0$ is exact (constant-sheaf exactness is clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties]). Tensoring it with the flat $B_T$ gives $0\to B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_T\to(R/\varpi^n)_T\to0$. Thus $[B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_T]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ is a free resolution of the quotient, and is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The quotient tower has epimorphic transitions, so [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] identifies its ordinary limit $B_T$ with its derived limit, through the quotient maps; hence $B_T[0]$ and its finite sums and shifts are complete. We use [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction] for closure of complete complexes under cones and for detecting an isomorphism by its residue reduction. Transport these assertions to the quotient-tower coefficient presentation used here. On the equivalent coefficient-sized site, [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] compares completed and constant coefficients on complete objects, preserving the actual quotient maps and derived reduction comparisons. Match the DVR coefficient ring through its canonical integer-ring identification, and the completed coefficient through the universal property of the inverse limit of its finite quotients. At each finite level the constant finite sheaf identifies with the continuous finite-valued function sheaf by sheafifying its clopen fibres. The tower comparisons commute with the projections, so their limit isomorphism identifies the completeness augmentation and its Roos triangle. These compatibility comparisons transport the continuous-coefficient cone and Nakayama conclusions to the recorded quotient-tower presentation; they are part of this step to formalize, rather than definitional identifications.

proof.text: Use the supplied zero-differential residue model. Its supplied term isomorphisms identify it with finite powers of the residue unit, with explicit vanishing outside [a,a+d]. Projectivity of the unit and its finite powers on the weakly contractible affine follows from [lem-sf-weakly-contractible-unit-projective]. For each site object V, the exact pullback comparison identifies the restricted residue with the termwise pullback of R. This has the same explicit bounds. Pullback of the regular module is the regular module by its tensor-unit comparison, and exact additive pullback preserves finite biproducts, so its terms remain finite free. The bounded flat model calculation gives the required Tor interval for this restricted residue, for every test module and every K-flat resolution, by the tensor comparison. Apply [lem-sf-complete-residue-cohomology-bounds] to obtain H^(a+d+1)(K)=0. Thus the stronger localized hypothesis is to be proved from this supplied model, not assumed from the global predicate.

Put $r=r_b$ and $P=B_U^{\oplus r}$. The free quotient resolution $F=[B_U\xrightarrow{\varpi}B_U]$ in step 1 computes residue tensor even for an unbounded representative of $M$: choose a K-flat resolution $M^{\flat}\to M$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; the maps $M^{\flat}\otimes F\to M^{\flat}\otimes k_U$ and $M^{\flat}\otimes F\to M\otimes F$ are quasi-isomorphisms by K-flatness of the two factors, the latter provided by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Consequently it yields the distinguished triangle $M\xrightarrow{\varpi}M\to M_1\to M[1]$. Its long exact sequence, supplied by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], gives a surjection $H^b(M)\to H^b(M_1)$ because $H^{b+1}(M)=0$. Exact evaluation on $U$ lifts the chosen $r$ basis sections of $H^b(M_1)$ to sections of $H^b(M)$, and then to cycles of a representative of $M$. These cycles define $f:P[-b]\to M$ inducing that basis on $H^b(M_1)$. By the Hom calculation of the supplied residue model its reduction $f_1:k_U^r[-b]\to M_1$, under the zero-differential residue model chosen there, is exactly the inclusion of the degree-$b$ summand: a map from $k_U^r[-b]$ into that model has only its degree-$b$ component, determined by $H^b(f_1)$.

source.place: Tag 09C3 (lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex), lifting the top-degree generators to a derived map; basis choice replaces the arbitrary top-degree surjection in the general-ring proof

proof.text: Complete $f$ to a triangle $P[-b]\to M\to L\xrightarrow{\delta}P[-b+1]$. The complex $L$ is complete by [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction]. Derived reduction is an exact triangulated functor by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so $L_1$ is the cone of $f_1$. Under the supplied residue decomposition this cone is the direct sum of $\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_U^{r_q}[-q]$ and the two-term identity complex on $k_U^r$, the latter contracted by the identity in the reverse direction. Thus $L_1\simeq\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_U^{r_q}[-q]$. Use this displayed lower zero-differential finite-free complex as W. Its actual terms vanish outside [a,b-1], and the contraction gives its isomorphism with the residue of L. The passage from this model to the shorter recorded Tor interval is proved separately in the parent induction, not asserted here. When $a=b$, this residue is zero, so $L=0$ by the same derived Nakayama lemma; then $f$ is an isomorphism, and $P[-a]$ is the required one-term free model. If $r=0$ the same calculation has $P=0$ and still decreases the interval.

theorem complete_residue_top_cell
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsAffine S)
    (hweak : (Scheme.ProEt.topology S).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1}
      (Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E S))
    (hcomplete : IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted.{u, u} l E S K)
    (a : ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    (hTor : HasProEtaleTorAmplitude S
      (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1)
      ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K) a (a + d))
    (R : CochainComplex
      (proEtaleRingModules S (proEtaleConstantRing S
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1))) ℤ)
    (hR : ∀ i j : ℤ, R.d i j = 0)
    (hRfree : ∀ q : ℤ, ∃ N : ℕ, Nonempty
      (R.X q ≅ ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ SheafOfModules.unit.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
        (integralCoefficientSheaf.{u, u} l E S 0)))
    (hRbound : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ a + d < q → IsZero (R.X q))
    (eR : Nonempty (((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj R)) :
    ∃ T : CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle
        (DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E S)),
      T ∈ distTriang _ ∧
      Nonempty (T.obj₂ ≅ K) ∧
      (∃ P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E S) ℤ,
        P.IsStrictlyGE (a + d) ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE (a + d) ∧
        (∀ r : ℤ, ∃ N : ℕ, Nonempty
          (P.X r ≅ ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ SheafOfModules.unit.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
            (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E S))) ∧
        Nonempty (T.obj₁ ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)) ∧
      IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted.{u, u} l E S T.obj₃ ∧
      (d = 0 → IsZero T.obj₃) ∧
      (∀ d' : ℕ, d = d' + 1 →
        ∃ W : CochainComplex
            (proEtaleRingModules S (proEtaleConstantRing S
              (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1))) ℤ,
          W.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ W.IsStrictlyLE (a + d') ∧
          (∀ i j : ℤ, W.d i j = 0) ∧
          (∀ q : ℤ, ∃ N : ℕ, Nonempty
            (W.X q ≅ ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ SheafOfModules.unit.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
              (integralCoefficientSheaf.{u, u} l E S 0))) ∧
          Nonempty (((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj T.obj₃) ≅
            DerivedCategory.Q.obj W))
